name: Southern Crossing
label: Southern Crossing
about_prose: Southern Crossing is one of the 13 neighborhood districts the City of Bend officially recognizes, established by Bend City Council on February 19, 2003, the fifth district to be formalized under that designation. It covers 882.9 acres and straddles the Deschutes River just south of downtown, bounded by the Bend Parkway (US-97) to the east, Simpson and Arizona Avenues to the north, Powers Road to the south, and Brookswood Boulevard and the river corridor to the west. The river runs through the middle of the neighborhood rather than along its edge, and the Old Mill District, Bend's largest concentration of shops, restaurants, and live entertainment, sits inside the same boundary instead of a drive away. There is no HOA here. Membership in the Southern Crossing Neighborhood Association is automatic for any resident 18 or older or business operator within the boundary, no dues required, with a volunteer board serving staggered two-year terms.

That retail core sits on an industrial site. Shevlin-Hixon Lumber Company built a mill on the river's west bank in 1916, and Brooks-Scanlon Lumber Company built its own Mill A on the east bank the same year, later adding the larger Mill B upstream in 1922. At their peak the two mills ranked among the largest pine sawmills in the world and each employed more than 2,000 workers. Shevlin-Hixon closed in 1950, and Brooks-Scanlon bought the site and shut it down four months later. Brooks-Scanlon's own Mill A closed in 1983, and Mill B kept running in reduced form until 1993. Developer Bill Smith and William Smith Properties bought the abandoned mill site in 1993 and opened the first shops in 1994, keeping the three original mill smokestacks standing as landmarks rather than tearing them down. The Bend Parkway and what is now the Hayden Homes Amphitheater, an outdoor venue that holds about 8,000 people, opened in 2001 and closed out the shift from lumber town to riverfront district.

The park anchoring the neighborhood's north end carries an older name than the mills. In the 1870s, rancher John Young Todd named his property on this stretch of the Deschutes Farewell Bend, for the place pioneers said goodbye to an easy river crossing before the dry high desert began. When the settlement applied for a post office in 1886, the U.S. Post Office Department shortened the name to Bend because Farewell Bend was already in use elsewhere. The townsite was platted in 1904, and the city incorporated the following January under that shortened name.

Day to day, the neighborhood runs on its parks and its trail. Farewell Bend Park, 22 acres at 1000 SW Reed Market Road, was acquired by the Bend Park and Recreation District in 1990 and has a lumber-mill-themed playground, a small beach and boat launch, a boardwalk along the river, and picnic shelters, open 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. The paved Deschutes River Trail runs the length of the park and connects north to the Old Mill District and south to South Canyon Bridge. Blakely Park, a smaller 3.4-acre park on Brookswood Boulevard named for the historic Old Blakely road, adds a playground and half-court closer to the neighborhood's western edge. Kids here are zoned into Bend-La Pine Schools: Pine Ridge Elementary on Hollygrape Street, Cascade Middle School on Mountaineer Way, and Caldera High School, which opened in 2021 as the district's newest high school and was rezoned to take in Southern Crossing students.

Southern Crossing was never platted as a single subdivision, so the housing stock is a genuine mix. Older river-adjacent homes sit near newer infill on the 124 vacant lots the neighborhood association still tracks, with multifamily and commercial parcels woven through rather than separated out. That mix is also the honest trade-off. The same boundary that includes the Old Mill District's retail and entertainment core also includes 452 active business licenses and 74 vacation home rentals, and parts of the neighborhood sit against Parkway noise, summer amphitheater traffic, and a steady flow of visitors headed to the shops and the river, in a way a purely residential neighborhood set back from the Parkway does not. It fits someone who wants river and downtown access built into daily life more than someone looking for a quiet cul-de-sac.

amenities.name: Farewell Bend Park
amenities.description: A 22-acre park along the Deschutes at 1000 SW Reed Market Road with a lumber-mill-themed Kiwanis playground, a river beach, a canoe launch, a picnic shelter, and a Deschutes River Trail connection north to the Old Mill District and south to South Canyon Bridge.

amenities.name: Blakely Park
amenities.description: A 3.4-acre neighborhood park at 1155 Brookswood Blvd with a large playground, a half-court, shade trees, and paved paths, named for the historic Old Blakely road.

amenities.name: Old Mill District
amenities.description: A riverfront retail and entertainment district on the former lumber-mill site within Southern Crossing, with shops, restaurants, the Tower Theatre, and direct Deschutes River Trail access.

amenities.name: Pine Ridge Elementary
amenities.description: A Bend-La Pine Schools K-5 at 19840 Hollygrape Street serving much of the district.

amenities.name: Caldera High School
amenities.description: Bend-La Pine Schools' newest high school, opened fall 2021 at 60925 SE 15th Street, rezoned to serve Southern Crossing students.

drive_times.note: About 2 miles north via SW Bond Street
